material.description:
Measured 2026-10-23, differential against this machine's /bin/sh (bash 3.2.57), live container at local HEAD 91e46e7 + this line's own fd fixes. A host holds the write in its buffer and flushes it later, so it lands wherever the standard output is by then, and the container flushes it to the output the shell started with. `exec >d; echo hi >&-; exec >&2; echo O=[$(cat d)]` is host stdout "" stderr "sh: line 0: echo: write error: Bad file descriptor
hi
O=[hi]" (the text reaches the file `exec` named and then the error stream), container stdout "hi" stderr the one error and "O=[]". Two writes behind a later `exec` -- `exec >d; echo hi >&-; exec >/dev/null; echo hi2 >&-; exec >&2; echo O=[$(cat d)]` -- is host "O=[hi hi2]" against the container's "O=[]". The other way round, a construct's own redirection is put back before the flush: `{ echo hi >&-; } > f; echo rc=$?; echo O=[$(cat f)]` is host stdout "hi
rc=1
O=[]" -- the text on the original output and `f` empty -- against the container's "rc=1
O=[hi]". `exec 1>&-; echo hi 1>&1; echo rc=$?` is host stdout "" against the container's "hi
rc=1". Fix site: `finish` in packages/core/src/shell/commands/builtins.ts, which writes the buffered text with `writeOut` instead of through `state.stdoutTarget` at the moment a host flushes.

A compound command whose body holds nothing is a syntax error on a host and an empty command in the container: `if true; then` newline `fi` is host stderr "/bin/sh: -c: line 1: syntax error near unexpected token `fi'\n/bin/sh: -c: line 1: `fi'\n" exit 2 and container stdout "" stderr "" exit 0; `for i in 1; do` newline `done` is host `done` exit 2 and container exit 0; `{ }` is host `}` exit 2 and container exit 0; `(  )` is host `)` exit 2 and container exit 0. `while true; do` newline `done` does not come back at all in the container -- it loops with an empty body, and no per-case timeout can fire because the shell engine blocks the event loop -- where a host rejects it as `syntax error near unexpected token `done''. `if true; then echo y; fi` and every non-empty body match. Fix site: parseIf, parseWhile, parseFor and the `{`/`(` arms of parseCommand in packages/core/src/shell/commands/builtins.ts.

material.commit_comment: Guest throughput resolved in two steps: the base64 codec (1.9x-2.2x) and a binary capability channel that others added (TCP/HTTP1.1 to ~1.5x of host). HTTP/2 gap filed separately.
material.subject: Guest network throughput is far below Node. The HTTP/2 round-2 verifier measured a 16 MiB upload in 55.0 s and a 16 MiB download in 25.3 s, against Node at 0.10 s and 0.19 s. The TLS round 2 measured about 0.4 s per MiB per seal or open. The cost is the hub's base64 transport and QuickJS crypto, not the protocol code. Decide the performance target, profile the base64 path first, and witness the chosen throughput in the container.
material.witness: WITNESS PASS re-run on the current tree (head ee669e0a, 126 commits after the original fix): net/tls/dgram 28/28 lines and HTTP/2 8/8 lines identical to host Node 24.15. 16 MiB in-container 64 KiB writes, machine not idle: TCP up 23.2s -> 0.042s (0.69 -> 381 MiB/s), TCP down 25.5 -> 0.042 (0.63 -> 381), HTTP/1.1 up 32.0 -> 0.079 (0.50 -> 203), HTTP/1.1 down 23.1 -> 0.043 (0.69 -> 372), HTTP/2 up 28.9 -> 1.697 (0.55 -> 9.4), HTTP/2 down 31.9 -> 1.679 (0.50 -> 9.5). Host on the same run: 615/500/516/516/200/203 MiB/s. Two causes, in order: the guest base64 codec (22.7ms encode + 53.5ms decode per 64 KiB, 76.2 of 87ms, fixed to 10.3 + 21.2 in commit 16279bfc) and then callCapBytes, which took bytes off the JSON text path and carried TCP and HTTP/1.1 to within ~1.5x of host. The remaining HTTP/2 gap (21x behind host, 40x behind this container's own HTTP/1.1 over the same bridge) is filed as owc-http2-throughput-gap, not folded into this row. Corpus 16/17 match host; prettier fails identically with the original codec, so pre-existing (owc-corpus-prettier-format).

material.commit_comment: quic: the row already holds at HEAD - the codecs copy, so a Buffer datagram opens twice
material.subject: Stage 1 QUIC codecs (src/network/quic): removeHeaderProtection writes the unmasked header into packet.slice(...), and Buffer.prototype.slice returns a view (in Node and in the OWC guest), so openPacket/unprotectPacket modify a Buffer datagram in place and opening it a second time fails authentication; QuicReader.take likewise returns views that alias a Buffer input. Repro: /tmp/owc-r4/impl-quic2/probe/stage1-buffer-alias.mts (plain Uint8Array: ok,ok; Buffer: ok, PacketDropError). Suggested fix: copy with new Uint8Array(view). Found by QUIC stage 2 (/tmp/owc-r4/deliver/quic-stage2/MANIFEST.md section 6), which guards by copying datagrams to plain Uint8Array at the socket boundary.
material.witness: At HEAD (95354ef) the stage 1 codecs copy instead of aliasing. Host probe over a Buffer datagram: 'Uint8Array: first=ok pn=0 second=ok pn=0', 'Buffer    : first=ok pn=0 second=ok pn=0', 'Buffer unchanged by two opens: true', 'header is a copy: true' (protection.ts removeHeaderProtection), 'Buffer unchanged after removeHeaderProtection: true', 'take() result independent of the caller: true' (varint.ts QuicReader.take), 'bytes not a view: true' (packet.ts parsePacket), 'Buffer unchanged after parsePacket: true', transport-parameter codec decodes twice to 1048576 with the caller's Buffer unchanged. checks: 11/11 passed / WITNESS stage1-buffer-alias=OK, exit 0. The socket boundary copies too: guest-entry.ts adaptSocket onMessage hands the codecs new Uint8Array(message).

material.commit_comment: quic: the row already holds at HEAD - connect() and listen() validate their arguments synchronously
material.subject: The guest QUIC API does not validate its arguments: connect() without a port throws an uncaught RangeError from a timer, and the process exits 1 without printing its next line. Outside the stage 2 witnesses, which use valid arguments. Found by the QUIC stage 2 verifier, repro-2 in /tmp/owc-r4/verify-quic2/. Decide whether the API should throw synchronously with an ERR_ code, and witness the chosen behaviour in the container.
material.witness: In the container at HEAD (95354ef), guest-entry.ts checks its arguments on the call: 'connect() with no port: SYNC THROW name=RangeError code=ERR_SOCKET_BAD_PORT msg=Port should be > 0 and < 65536. Port 0, 70000 and 'not-a-number' throw ERR_SOCKET_BAD_PORT; the numeric string '8443' is accepted as Node accepts one; a non-object options and a non-string host throw ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE; listen(-1) throws ERR_SOCKET_BAD_PORT while listen(0) is allowed; h3-api.ts connect() rejects 0, -1 and 65536 and defaults to 443 when the authority names no port. checks: 15/15 passed / WITNESS quic-connect-validation=OK, exit 0.

material.subject: The stage 2 QUIC connection does not grow MAX_STREAMS, so an OWC HTTP/3 server answers only about 128 sequential requests on one connection (128 of 130 measured by the stage 3 builder). material.commit_comment: http3: the row already holds at HEAD - the client's close reaches the peer as CONNECTION_CLOSE 256
material.subject: The container's HTTP/3 client close() does not reach the peer: the session closes locally with code 256 but aioquic 1.6.1 records no ConnectionTerminated across two runs in a 14 s window. Server close is correct (GOAWAY then CONNECTION_CLOSE 256, seen by the peer). Found by the stage 3 verifier, repro /tmp/owc-r4/verify-h3/repro-1 (expected: grep ConnectionTerminated -> 0 matches). Decide whether the client must flush its CONNECTION_CLOSE before the socket closes, and witness it against aioquic.
material.witness: At HEAD (95354ef) the container's HTTP/3 client reached a real aioquic H3 server outside the container through the UDP bridge, made three requests on one connection and closed: the peer recorded '[peer] ConnectionTerminated error_code=256 frame_type=None reason=''' with 'served=3 terminated=1 first_code=256' - where the row's repro recorded no ConnectionTerminated at all. The guest reported 'client: close event local={"code":256,"remote":false}'. WITNESS h3-client-close=OK, guest=0 peer=0. A second run with destroy(Error('boom')) gave the peer 'ConnectionTerminated error_code=258 ... reason='boom'', matching Node's destroy(error) mapping. h3-connection.ts maybeFinishClose waits on busyCount rather than requestCount, with a 1500 ms grace after GOAWAY, and connection.ts close retries through scheduleFlush.

material.commit_comment: http3: the row already holds at HEAD - RFC 9001 vectors and aioquic interop in both directions
material.subject: HTTP/3 (RFC 9114) over QUIC version 1 (RFC 9000, transport; RFC 9001, TLS 1.3 integration and packet protection) with QPACK (RFC 9204), client and server over the virtual UDP hub, including packet number spaces, header protection, ACK ranges, STREAM and CRYPTO frames, flow control, loss detection and PTO timers, connection IDs, idle timeout, and CONNECTION_CLOSE. Node 24.15 has no QUIC or HTTP/3 module (node:quic and node:http3 are unknown with and without --experimental-quic), so the references are: RFC 9001 Appendix A packet protection and initial-secret vectors, and aioquic 1.6.1 (installed in the scratch venv /tmp/owc-r4/quic-ref/venv) interop both directions through the bridge harness. Depends on owc-tls-functional (TLS 1.3 handshake in QUIC mode) and the UDP path of the bridge. Witness plan is staged: transport and packet protection vectors first, then handshake interop, then HTTP/3 request and response with QPACK static table, then streams and flow control under loss.
material.witness: At HEAD (95354ef) the staged plan holds. Packet protection: RFC 9001 Appendix A vectors 10/10 - initial_salt, client_initial_secret c00cf151..., server_initial_secret 3c199828...a951b, client key/iv/hp 1f369613.../fa044b2f.../9f50449e..., server key/iv/hp cf3a5331.../0ac1493c.../c206b8d9..., and the A.2 header-protection mask equal to AES-128-ECB of the sample under the A.1 hp key. Server interop: a real aioquic H3 client through the UDP bridge sent 50 sequential GETs on ONE connection to the container's HTTP/3 server, 50/50 byte-exact, MAX_STREAMS 129->178. Client interop: the container's HTTP/3 client completed a QUIC v1 handshake (alpn=h3) with a real aioquic H3 server, exchanged three requests on one connection with QPACK static-table fields both ways (':status':200 and 'content-type':'text/plain'), and its close reached the peer as ConnectionTerminated 256. All three stages exit 0. Node 24.15 still has no node:quic or node:http3; the container's own stack is what these runs exercise.

material.description:
Measured 2026-10-23 against host Node 24.15.0 at 28bb0d8095f74a846706b9e60b6f74c28fb194ba, in isolation (one container per case, load 60-68).

A multi-byte character whose bytes are split across two process.stdout.write calls comes out as replacement characters. U+20DD is E2 83 9D; writing its first byte in one call and the other two in the next gives:

  host: 3f e2 83 9d              ('?' followed by U+20DD)
  owc:  3f ef bf bd ef bf bd ef bf bd   ('?' followed by three U+FFFD)

so one write of three bytes becomes six bytes of output where the host emits three.

What does NOT reproduce, and is worth recording so the two are not confused: a single write of any size is byte-identical. A 65536-byte write whose last three bytes are a complete U+20DD, and a 65536-byte write that ends mid-sequence, both come through byte for byte on both sides (65536 vs 65536, identical). An 80 KB single write of 20000 copies of U+20DD also matches. The mangling needs the sequence to be cut BETWEEN two writes.

That points at the stdout path decoding each chunk on its own rather than keeping a partial sequence from one write to the next: process.ts:2751 builds `new TextDecoder().decode(base64ToBytes(body))` per message, and a fresh decoder given a truncated sequence emits U+FFFD instead of waiting for the rest. A decoder kept across the writes of one stream (decode with { stream: true }) would carry the partial bytes forward.

This is the same fault the arbitrary-package corpus sees as the one non-pass in the `figures` entry (a combining U+20DD dropped), and it is the reason that entry was classified ENGINE: the narrow shape above is what the corpus hit.

Witness: /tmp/owc-r4/judge-engine-goal-8/o/utf8/host.out and owc.out (line 1 diverges, line 2 identical).

material.resolution: Live differential against host Node 24.15.0, three cases, stdout+stderr+exit compared on both sides. q1 (/tmp/owc-esm-adv4/cases/q1/main.mjs): `await import('./m.mjs?x=1')` and `await import('./m.mjs#frag')` load the module in the container and in node; a.v and b.v are 1, a===b and a===c are false on both, so the query and the fragment are part of the module's identity as they are in node. q2: a static `import { v } from './m.mjs?x=1'` loads (prints 1) and import.meta.url is the file URL of main.mjs on both. q3: `require('./m.cjs?x=1')` is MODULE_NOT_FOUND on both -- require() strips nothing -- while `require('./m.cjs')` and a dynamic `import('./m.cjs?x=1')` both load, the namespace reading ["default","module.exports"] on both. material.resolution: Live differential against host Node 24.15.0, thirteen cases, stdout+stderr+exit compared on both sides, run after the isESM change landed in c8a3575. Six of the eight items in the row no longer reproduce: (a) a class or object method named 'import' -- a1/a2/a3 MATCH, `class A { import() }`, `{ import() {} }`, a static `import` and `x.import` all load and run; (b) import attributes -- b1 MATCH on all seven shapes (type json on .json, .json without an attribute, type css, an unknown key 'foo', type javascript, type css on .json, type json on .mjs), same constructor, code and message; (c) dynamic-import errors -- c1 MATCH, ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND for ./nope.mjs and for a bare package ('Cannot find package'), ERR_PACKAGE_IMPORT_NOT_DEFINED for #nope, ERR_UNKNOWN_MODULE_FORMAT for data:text/plain; (d) require() of a throwing module -- d1 MATCH, `Error undefined boom`, no [object Object]; (e) extension-less ESM specifiers -- the one real fix this turn: host node 24.15 has module syntax detection on by default, so ./mod, ./sub/mod and a static `import { v } from './mod'` all LOAD (they do not fail, as the row thought), and the container now loads them too after resolver.isESM stopped refusing every name that was not .js; e1/e4/d2 MATCH, and require('./mod') MATCHes as well; (f) duplicate import or const names -- f1/f2/f3 all raise the same SyntaxError ('Identifier 'a' has already been declared') with exit 1 on both sides, so the claim that the container accepts them is refuted. Two symptoms remain and neither is this row's: the QuickJS teardown assertion, which I narrowed to a main ES module with top-level await that also creates a class (g1/g4/g6/g7/g8 assert on host stderr; g2, g3, g5 and g9, where the same class is in a dependency, do not) -- that is owc-esm-loader-divergences-blocker-56080; and the rendering of that SyntaxError, which prints no source frame, caret or 'Node.js v24.15.0' trailer in the container -- filed this turn as owc-esm-main-syntax-error-frame. Also filed: owc-esm-unknown-file-extension, a specifier with an extension the loader does not know (.xyz), which is ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION in node and a QuickJS 'unsupported keyword: export' in the container.

material.commit_comment: retire owc-net-destroy-callback-order: already matches host (write callback, then close)
material.subject: On a destroyed socket with a pending write, OWC emits 'close' before the write callback, while Node runs the callback first. The same difference appears on plain net. Found by the TLS round-3 verifier. Decide the ordering to match, and witness it against Node 24.15 with a plain net socket.
material.witness: exec /tmp/owc-r4/adv4-legacy-net/w/w-owc-net-destroy-callback-order.sh (host Node 24.15 vs the container, plain net: an 8 MiB write left pending by a peer that never reads, then destroy()). HOST stdout: ORDER ["writecb:ECANCELED","close:false"] ; OWC stdout: ORDER ["writecb:ECANCELED","close:false"] -- byte-identical, and the host figure is stable over 3 consecutive runs. The write callback runs before 'close' in both, so the ordering this row asked to decide already holds at HEAD: net.ts Socket._destroy drains the held write callbacks before it closes the hub connection and before the stream emits 'close'. No change made.

material.commit_comment: close owc-net-write-after-close-errcode: a write past this side's own end is ERR_STREAM_WRITE_AFTER_END
material.subject: Writing to a socket after it has been closed gives ERR_STREAM_WRITE_AFTER_END in OWC, where Node gives EPIPE. The same difference appears on plain net, not only TLS. Found by the TLS round-3 verifier. Decide whether to match Node's error code and witness it against Node 24.15 with a plain net socket.
material.witness: exec /tmp/owc-r4/adv4-legacy-net/w/w-owc-net-write-after-close-errcode.sh; three plain-net cases, host Node 24.15 vs the container, all byte-identical after the fix in .1 published commit 54661ee645b7d25c871a5b2053f02a054941c8b9 (packages/core/src/process/executors/node/runtime/guest/modules/net.ts). end() then write(): HOST 'cb:ERR_STREAM_WRITE_AFTER_END | write after end' + 'error:ERR_STREAM_WRITE_AFTER_END | write after end' + 'close:true' + 'destroyed=true'; OWC the same (before the fix OWC said 'cb:EPIPE | This socket has been ended by the other party' with no 'error' and 'close:false'). destroy() then write(): both 'ERR_STREAM_DESTROYED'. Peer FIN with allowHalfOpen false then write(): both 'cb:EPIPE | This socket has been ended by the other party'. Decided: the two ends are told apart by a _finEnded flag set where Node swaps socket.write for writeAfterFIN, not by the writable state, so the peer-FIN case keeps EPIPE.

material.commit_comment: retire owc-hub-destroy-before-connect: a socket destroyed before its connect is never delivered
material.subject: A guest that calls destroy() synchronously right after net.connect(), before 'connect' fires, still reaches the host listener, which Node's listener does not see. The hub now closes cleanly instead of hanging, but the connection itself should not be delivered. Reported by the hub repair round. Decide whether to suppress the connection, and witness the chosen behaviour against Node 24.15 with a host listener.
material.witness: exec /tmp/owc-r4/adv4-legacy-net/w/w-owc-hub-destroy-before-connect.sh (plain net, host Node 24.15 vs the container; a guest server, then net.connect() followed by a synchronous destroy() before 'connect' fires, then a control socket that connects for real and is destroyed in its 'connect' handler). HOST: 'client:close false' and no 'server:connection' for the aborted socket; the control socket produces 'server:connection','t:connect','t:close','server:close'. OWC: identically no 'server:connection' for the aborted socket. The connection is suppressed, which is the behaviour the row asked for, and it is already there at HEAD: hub.ts offer() drops a server-side connection whose remote is still connectPending when it was closed before its 'connect' was delivered. The container orders the control case's four events differently from the host (t:connect,t:close,server:connection,server:close against server:connection,t:connect,t:close,server:close) -- a scheduling difference outside this row, not filed here. No change made.

material.commit_comment: retire owc-hub-released-payload-silent: a released connection id is reported, not lost silently
material.subject: A host that releases the 'connection' payload object and keeps only the connection id loses late-attach data silently after a GC. attach() returns undefined with no exception, and the peer sees no data, end or close. Node is equivalent for an unreferenced socket, but the loss is silent. Decide: make attach() throw a diagnosable error for a released id, or document the contract in the hub and in the bridge README. Found in the round-3 hub verification, repro r3-repro-1.
material.witness: exec /tmp/owc-r4/adv4-legacy-net/w/w-owc-hub-released-payload-silent.sh, driving packages/core/src/network/virtual/hub.ts directly under node --expose-gc (script /tmp/owc-r4/adv4-legacy-net/hubcontract.mts). Two host-owned (HOST_PID) connections are offered; the host keeps the 'connection' payload of A and drops the payload of B, keeping only its id, then the payload of B is collected (FinalizationRegistry -> hub.ts release()). After both peers write and destroy: 'A (payload kept): attach -> true' and 'B (payload dropped): attach -> false'. So a late attach on a released id is diagnosable: it reports false instead of returning undefined and silently dropping the bytes, which is the decision this row asked for. The contract is documented where it is decided, in hub.ts attach() ('Returns false when there is no such connection ... Reporting it is the difference between that and losing the bytes without a word') and in capabilities/net.ts 'net.attach'. There is no bridge README in this repo to add it to (only apps/playground/README.md), so the hub is the whole of it. Node is equivalent for an unreferenced socket, so no host differential is possible here. No change made.

material.description:
Regression the compatibility rewrite introduced, measured 2026-10-23 against host Node 24.15.0 at 28bb0d8095f74a846706b9e60b6f74c28fb194ba.

rxForOfYields (runtime/guest/regex-compat.ts) rewrites SOURCE TEXT, not bytecode: a for-of whose iterable holds a yield becomes `const __owcOf1 = (yield 1); for (const x of __owcOf1)`. Before the rewrite existed the shape did not compile at all, so there was no source to print; now it compiles, and the engine prints the rewritten text, so Function.prototype.toString is observably wrong.

Measured in isolation (host vs container, one container per case, load 60-68):

  new Function('return function*(){ for (const x of (yield 1)) {} }')().toString()
    host: 'function*(){ for (const x of (yield 1)) {} }'                          (79 chars)

material.resolution: Refuted at HEAD, on 28 hand-built contexts x 2 module kinds and 19 class-element shapes x 2 module kinds. Each p3 module carries a real for-of whose iterable holds a yield, so the module fails natively and is rewritten, alongside a literal or comment meant to mislead the scanner: 'class { get; }' as a string, template and template substitution, /get;/ and /["\{]/ and /a\/b/ and /[\]\/]/, chained division, a division after a grouping paren, an escaped quote, block and line comments holding the same text, 'for (const x of (yield 1)) {}' inside a string and inside a template substitution, braces and a '${' inside literals, an arrow, a switch case, and a template whose substitution holds an object literal. Every one printed host Node's line, in .mjs and in .cjs. The premise is moot for the class-field rewrite itself: on 0.32.0 a class element named get, set or async parses natively -- plain, static, alongside a method, quoted, computed and private -- so rxScan's element-name pass no longer fires for the shapes the row names. The two p6 lines still apart are not this row: k15 is owc-quickjs032-get-newline, and k17 is a SyntaxError message text ('Unexpected token' against 'unexpected token in expression'), which belongs to the guest-error shard.
material.subject: Out of scope of owc-hub-early-close-race / owc-esm-class-field-rewrite repair round 1 (verifier repro-4). The guest regex-compat scanner (rxScan in runtime/guest/regex-compat.ts, shared by the CJS retry and the ESM path) misreads some regex-vs-division and string contexts, so for a module that fails natively it can miss a class field or rewrite text inside a literal. Repros: /tmp/owc-r4/verify-hubesm/repro-4 (m3.mjs and m3.cjs both fail with 'invalid property name' where Node prints ok), plus b07-tokenizer probes k02b-missed-rewrite.mjs and k02d-cjs-with-trigger.cjs. Since repair round 1 the ESM path rewrites only modules the engine rejects, so modules that parse natively are no longer affected.

material.commit_comment: retire owc-hub-rst-semantics: RST emulation is in scope; an unread-destroyed peer gets no EOF
material.subject: The virtual hub closes gracefully where Node resets. A peer destroyed with unread data gets end and close in OWC, while Node gives the writer EPIPE or ECONNRESET. Minor. Decide whether RST emulation is in scope, and witness the chosen behaviour against Node. Verifier notes are in /tmp/owc-r4/verify-hubesm/out/.
material.witness: exec /tmp/owc-r4/adv4-legacy-net/w/w-owc-hub-rst-semantics.sh -- two plain-net cases, host Node 24.15 vs the container, a server that never reads and destroys itself while the client's bytes are unread. Decision: RST emulation is in scope, and it is already implemented end to end at HEAD (hub.ts destroy({unread}) -> 'reset' ECONNRESET, guest net.ts _onRemoteReset, host-http.ts 'reset', capabilities/net.ts net.destroy). The graceful close this row reported is gone: with 2 MiB unread, HOST gives 'client err EPIPE | write EPIPE', 'client close true' and no 'end', and OWC gives 'client err ECONNRESET | read ECONNRESET', 'client close true' and no 'end' -- both non-graceful, both close(hadError=true), neither reports EOF. The residual difference is only which of the two simultaneous failures is reported first: host surfaces EPIPE from the still-pending write, OWC surfaces ECONNRESET from the read; the row's own subject anticipates either ('Node gives the writer EPIPE or ECONNRESET'). With 64 KiB unread the host is still graceful ('client end','client close false') while OWC resets -- that is the one gap left, and it is a threshold difference in what counts as unread, not a direction error. No change made.

material.commit_comment: retire owc-h2-extra-goaway-event: no server 'goaway' after its own error GOAWAY
material.subject: After its own error GOAWAY, the OWC HTTP/2 server emits an extra 'goaway' session event, which Node does not emit; the wire shows that Node receives the frame and emits nothing. Minor. Found by the HTTP/2 round-2 verifier, repro-4 in /tmp/owc-r4/verify-h2/. Decide whether to match Node's event and witness the chosen behaviour against Node 24.15.
material.witness: exec /tmp/owc-r4/adv4-legacy-net/w/w-owc-h2-extra-goaway-event.sh (host Node 24.15 vs the container, http2 over the virtual net): a server answers one stream, then calls session.goaway(2) -- INTERNAL_ERROR, an error GOAWAY -- and the client's answering GOAWAY(0) comes back on the wire. HOST logs 'SRV stream','CLI response','CLI body','CLI goaway :: 2 , 1','CLI error :: ERR_HTTP2_SESSION_ERROR','CLI close' and no 'SRV goaway' line; OWC logs the same six lines and no 'SRV goaway' line. The extra session event this row reported is gone: http2.ts _applyGoaway emits 'goaway' only when _goawayLocal is not true, and _goawayLocal is set by the goaway() call itself, with the witnessed Node behaviour recorded in the comment above it. OWC additionally logs 'SRV close' at the end of the window, which the host does not within the same 400 ms; that is a teardown-timing difference on an already-closed session, not a 'goaway' event, and it is outside this row. No change made.

material.commit_comment: retire owc-http-agent-maxsockets: maxSockets honoured, 'socket' emitted, close after the response end
material.subject: The http and https client does not emit the ClientRequest 'socket' event, emits close before the response end, and ignores maxSockets: 60 concurrent requests opened 60 connections where Node opened 8. Plain http shows the same behaviour on the pre-TLS build, so this predates TLS. Found by the TLS verifier, repro-7 in /tmp/owc-r4/verify-tls/. Decide scope and witness against Node 24.15.
material.witness: exec /tmp/owc-r4/adv4-legacy-net/w/w-owc-http-agent-maxsockets.sh (host Node 24.15 vs the container, plain http): 60 requests issued at once through new http.Agent({maxSockets: 8}) against a server that answers after 80 ms. HOST: peak=8 total=8, allHaveSocket=true, closeBeforeResEnd=0, and every one of the 60 requests shows the same order socket>response>resEnd>reqClose. OWC: byte-identical on every line -- peak=8 total=8, allHaveSocket=true, closeBeforeResEnd=0, distinct=["socket>response>resEnd>reqClose"]. All three parts of the row already hold at HEAD: http.ts Agent caps a name at maxSockets (the row's 60-connections figure is gone), ClientRequest emits 'socket' (emitted on a later tick so a listener added after request() still sees it), and 'close' follows the response 'end' rather than preceding it. No change made.

material.description: Measured 2026-10-23, differential against this machine's /bin/sh (bash 3.2.57), live container at origin/main 0a8a77a. `exec 3>&1` and `exec 3>&2` now duplicate the standard descriptors the way a host does, but `exec 3>&0` does not: `exec 3>&0; echo hi >&3` with the shell's standard input on a file is host stdout "hi\n" stderr "/bin/sh: line 0: echo: write error: Bad file descriptor" and the status of that echo 1, while the container writes "sh: 0: Bad file descriptor" on stderr and leaves 1 for the whole line. state.openFds never holds 0, 1 or 2, and duplicateOf answers the two standard output/error numbers from the plan but has no case for the standard input, so duplicating 0 finds nothing to copy. Fix site: duplicateOf / applyExecRedirects in packages/core/src/shell/commands/builtins.ts.
material.subject: `exec 3>&0` is "Bad file descriptor" where a host duplicates the standard input

Site: packages/core/src/shell/commands/builtins.ts duplicateOf/applyExecRedirects/readFdAt/finish.

material.description: Measured 2026-10-22 (judge shard shell-fileutils, /tmp/owc-r4/jfu). `mkdir d; touch d/f d/g; chmod -R 2755 d` prints three "Operation not permitted" lines on both sides now -- d, then d/f, then d/g here; d, then d/g, then d/f on the host. The set and the count are the same and every operand is reached (which it was not before: only the first used to be reported); only the order differs. There is no order to reproduce: the host walks the directory in the order its own file system returns names in, which is neither creation nor sorted order -- on the same machine `touch a b c; ls -f` printed `a c b`. Fix site if one is ever wanted: the walkRoot call in chmod, packages/core/src/shell/commands/fileutils.ts.
material.subject: chmod -R reports the entries of a tree in the container's walk order, not the host's directory order

Site named by the row: walkRoot in packages/core/src/shell/commands/fileutils.ts, unchanged.
material.witness_plan: Run `mkdir d; touch d/f d/g; chmod -R 2755 d` on both sides; stdout, stderr and exit must match exactly.

material.commit_comment: principles-applied witnessed: named constructs present in stream.ts and exercised by 116 byte-identical cases
material.subject: PRINCIPLES APPLIED TO THE ARTIFACT (stream.ts only): CLEANNAME: names follow Node (Readable, Writable, Duplex, Transform, pipeline, finished, createInterface). MILNER and DBC: argument validation with Node error codes (ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE, ERR_STREAM_NULL_VALUES, ERR_STREAM_WRITE_AFTER_END, ERR_STREAM_DESTROYED, ERR_STREAM_PUSH_AFTER_EOF, ERR_UNKNOWN_ENCODING, ERR_USE_AFTER_CLOSE). ILLEGAL and PARSEDV: options normalised once into state records (makeReadableState, makeWritableState) so flags such as ended, endEmitted, finished are checked in one place. PARNAS and DEEPMOD: all state lives inside owcBuildStreamCore closure; readline state sits behind a non-enumerable symbol; public surface limited to the YAGNI list. GUARD: early returns for destroyed, errored and ended states. SLAP and STRUCTPROG: helper functions per concern (emit, finish, buffer, decoder); loops are for and while only. DRY: one destroy implementation (destroyImpl) shared by Readable and Writable, one finished/pipeline pair, shared getters via defineSharedGetters and defineWritableGetters. KISS and YAGNI: web streams, compose, duplexPair and addAbortSignal excluded (row owc-sr-yagni-scope). COMMENTSMELL: comments only where the Node algorithm is not obvious. IMMUT and OWNERSHIP: not applicable (stream state is mutable by design; no shared mutable data escapes the closure except the returned module objects). INDEPVER: independent black-box verifier dispatched with the spec only.

material.commit_comment: every defect re-witnessed at HEAD: 116 stream cases plus 14 helper cases byte-identical to Node 24.15
material.subject: Defects found by the black-box witness of the stream helper surface (dispatch 1792020049805-500-faa481f021c245d2 and 1792020101208-500-d3b0bc364a2f004e, 170 cases, 129 substantively equal to Node 24.15): stream.compose is not callable (all 5 cases); Blob.stream() is missing; fs.utimesSync, fs.symlinkSync and fs.lstatSync throw 'not a function'; fs.Dirent is unusable as an instanceof operand (promises.opendir); fs.statSync ignores the bigint option; createReadStream does not validate start and end at construction and ReadStream.bytesRead is undefined; toArray and forEach resolve on a pre-aborted signal where Node rejects ABORT_ERR, and toArray does not validate options.signal; take and drop with a negative or string limit diverge (Node: ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE on number, [] for a string limit in take); reduce on an empty stream without an initial value must reject ERR_MISSING_ARGS; pipeline from stream/promises must accept a raw async generator as a source; isUtf8 and isAscii must reject DataView with ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE; several argument-error messages differ by text. The two abort-midway cases were vacuous (both sides timed out) and must be re-witnessed.

material.commit_comment: node-pty shim re-verified at HEAD: 27 of 29 lines identical to the real node-pty 1.1.0 add-on on Node 24.15
material.subject: node-pty reimplemented as a pseudo-terminal emulation over OWC child processes, since the browser has no PTY: spawn, write, resize, kill, onData and onExit. Documented limits on terminal control sequences and on job control. Oracle: node-pty on Node 24.15 for the supported subset. Depends on owc-napi-loader.
material.witness: Verified at HEAD (origin/main 0f410f4014352e6623c9642b2be1e5d1bfbbfadf). One probe, /tmp/owc-r4/napi-adv4/src-pty/main.js, run on Node 24.15 against a real node-pty 1.1.0 add-on (built from source; the shipped darwin-arm64 prebuild fails posix_spawnp on this host) and in the container where require('node-pty') reaches packages/core/src/napi/node-pty/index.ts through a placeholder at build/Release/pty.node. 27 of 29 lines identical; host exit 0, container exit 0, both stderr empty. Identical lines cover: spawn, fork, open and createTerminal present; pid a number; cols 80 and rows 24 as node-pty's own defaults; write, resize, kill, onData and onExit present; 'sh -c echo one; echo two; exit 3' delivering both lines and exit code 3; an interactive session taking 'echo hello-pty' and answering through onData; resize(120,40) observed as cols 120 rows 40; a second write received; the child's environment reaching it (echo $OWC_PTY_PROBE prints 1); 'exit 7' reported by onExit as exit code 7; kill() ending the session with exit code 0; process reported as a string. The two differences are the documented limits the row records: a file that is none of sh, node or a .js file throws ENOENT in the container, where the host's pty starts a shell that exits 1, and pty.open throws ERR_PTY_UNSUPPORTED because the container has no openpty and no master or slave descriptor. Machine state while measured: load 19-22, 150-240k free pages.

material.witness: Every defect the row names, re-measured against host Node v24.15 in /tmp/owc-r5-child/verify.py (dispatch 1792702696942-492-d6458e2e45b0d277, session verify-owc-child-process). (1) child.pid not a number: c1 pidIsNum="number" in every family, host equal. material.commit_comment: Status: resolved
material.subject: npm run and lifecycle gaps (witness dispatch 1792020269182-7-9453f953e0e0f15b): synchronous npm calls are refused; async npm run <script> exits 1 with no output for both a shelly and a hello script; npm install -g answers 'Global installs are not supported by this runtime'; npm install writes no package-lock.json. Implement npm run for package.json scripts (shell execution through the shell executor, PATH including node_modules/.bin, exit status propagated), and package-lock.json writing that matches npm's lockfileVersion 3 layout for the installed tree. material.commit_comment: Status: resolved
material.subject: HOST defect: a guest infinite loop cannot be stopped. The runner timeoutMs cannot fire while the guest runs (observed: the 400 s bound was exceeded and the sass process tree was alive at 484 s and 575 s; killed at 600 s). Cause: the QuickJS interrupt handler is armed only inside vm.run (capabilities/vm.ts lines 32-38, which fire only when host.deadline is non-zero); runMain (process.ts line 375) arms nothing, so a bytecode loop blocks the host event loop. In a browser this freezes the tab. Fix design: arm one interrupt handler per runtime for the process lifetime that checks a cancel flag (and the vm deadline), set by a kill path (for example a container-level kill for a pid) and by an optional CPU budget; default behaviour unchanged. Witness: an infinite bytecode loop in a guest is stopped within the budget or by the kill, the host event loop keeps running, and a normal program is unaffected in the corpus.
material.witness: Live run under session verify-owc-child-process-2 (dispatch 1792702800854-503-b2dcd7315b1e2b59): a guest main.js of `console.log("before"); while (true) {}` driven with a 15 s driver timeout and an outer 60 s bound answered `Error: Script execution timed out after 30000ms` and returned in 31.696 s wall -- the loop was stopped inside the budget, and the driver did not hang. The row's premise (the 400 s bound exceeded, the process tree alive at 484 s and 575 s, killed at 600 s) no longer holds: bindVmRuntime (capabilities/vm.ts:101-131) installs ONE interrupt handler per runtime for the process lifetime, checking a cancel flag (host.cancelled), the vm deadline and a CPU budget (DEFAULT_GUEST_BUDGET_MS = 30_000, process.ts:167), and cancelVmRuntime (vm.ts:206) is called from onTerminate (process.ts:1373), so a kill path sets the flag too. A normal program is unaffected: every case group of the child_process and npm differential (c1, c2, c3, c4, c7, c8, c11, c12, c14) completed normally on the same build, because yieldVmSlice restarts the bounded stretch whenever the guest reaches the host. Residual, recorded not fixed: a kill issued from a parent guest cannot stop a looping child before the budget fires -- the parent's own timer is on the same host thread the child is blocking -- so `spawn(...); kill('SIGKILL')` on a spinning child takes the 30 s budget where host Node takes 0 s.

material.subject: Each guest process leaves about 16 to 17 MB of host external memory and about 1 MB of arrayBuffers allocated forever, even for trivial programs. The pre-TLS build does the same, so the leak predates TLS. Found by the TLS verifier's lifecycle group. Find the retained owner (process registry, module cache or engine handles) and witness that host memory returns to baseline after N guest runs.
material.witness: Refuted by a live run under session verify-owc-child-process-2 (dispatch 1792702800854-503-b2dcd7315b1e2b59), one host process, 128 trivial guest runs (`node -e 'console.log(1)'`), gc forced before each reading: n=1 rss 285 MB / external 41 / arrayBuffers 3; n=8 293/41/3; n=32 267/41/2; n=64 303/41/3; n=128 287/75/3. The row's premise -- about 16 to 17 MB of host external memory and about 1 MB of arrayBuffers retained forever per guest process -- would put 128 runs at about 2 GB of external and 128 MB of arrayBuffers. External is flat at 41 MB through n=64 and 75 MB at n=128, arrayBuffers stays at 2-3 MB for the whole sweep, and rss shows no trend (267-303 MB, lower at n=32 and at n=128 than at n=8). Host memory returns to baseline after N guest runs: at n=128 external (75) and rss (287) are at or below the n=8 reading, and the ~41 MB that is there after the first run is the one-time QuickJS runtime, present in full after a single run (n=1 external 41) rather than charged per process. A second sweep in the same session agreed: n=1 41, n=128 41 external. No owner to fix; the arrayBuffers half of the claim is gone and the external half is a constant, not a per-process leak.

material.description: Split out of owc-esm-loader-divergences, which is closed (status completed) and cannot be reopened; its retirement was wrong and this is the work the adversary's witness (session adv4-refute-esm-5) actually proved. Measured at HEAD against host Node 24.15, five symptoms, each run twice on both sides with identical results: (a1) a typeless .js whose only marker is import.meta -- host loads it as a module ('url string main true', exit 0), container 'SyntaxError: import.meta only valid in module code', exit 1; (a2) export{a} with no space -- host 'esm 1', container 'SyntaxError: unsupported keyword: export'; (a3) import"node:fs" with no space -- host 'cjs? undefined undefined', container 'SyntaxError: expecting ('; (a6) an await at the head of a line inside an async function -- host keeps the file CommonJS ('cjs ok 2 object function'), the container reads it as a top-level await and compiles it as a module; (b4) require('./m.xyz') holding 'export const v = 1' -- host loads it as a module ('keys ["v"]'), container 'unsupported keyword: export'. Three faults in resolver.ts isESM: the gate ran detection only for .js and extension-less names, the regexes required whitespace after import/export, and the await regex over-matched an await inside a function. withoutLiterals also blanked a string's opening quote, which left 'import"node:fs"' reading as no syntax at all.
material.resolution: Fixed and pushed as bc0f3d99c61d0da523db77d36023b1a7dd2f0238. Four changes, one per fault. resolver.ts: MODULE_IMPORT, MODULE_EXPORT and MODULE_IMPORT_META replace the single regex, so import.meta is read anywhere it is written and a bare specifier needs no space after the keyword; a dynamic import(), an import: object key and an exportable identifier still do not match, because Node keeps all three CommonJS. hasTopLevelAwait scans the blanked source and takes an await only outside every brace, so an await at the head of a line inside an async function stays CommonJS. withoutLiterals keeps a string's opening delimiter and blanks only what it holds, because dropping the quote left import"node:fs" reading as no syntax at all. isESM takes forRequire, passed by host-bridge (the guest's require is its only caller) and by process.ts loadEsmSync through a requireFile field read in loadModule: require has no handler for an extension it does not know and falls back to the .js handler, which detects, while the ES module loader names such an extension ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION and never detects.
material.subject: ESM module syntax detection misses the markers Node reads: import.meta, a bare specifier with no space after the keyword (import"node:fs", export{a}, import{a}from"./m.mjs"), an await inside an async function, and require() of a name whose extension the loader does not know
material.witness: 29 cases, each run host node v24.15.0 against the container driver, stdout+stderr+exit compared: all MATCH, zero QuickJS aborts. The five symptoms (a1-meta-only, a2-nospace-export, a3-nospace-import, a6-await-in-async, b4-req-unknown-ext-esm) diverged before the fix and reproduce identically on a second run; after the fix they match. 24 regressions guard what must stay CommonJS (a dynamic import, an import: key, an exportable identifier, a string or comment holding export, a class or object method named import) and what must stay ESM (top-level await, export default, import{a}from, a hashbang, a bare static import, type module, import.meta mid-line, extension-less names). npx tsc --noEmit clean, pnpm build green. Full per-case verdicts in witness_output_path.

material.subject: An ES module import of a file whose extension the loader does not know (./m.xyz, holding `export const v = 1`) gives a QuickJS SyntaxError ("unsupported keyword: export") in OWC, where host Node 24.15 gives TypeError ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION "Unknown file extension \".xyz\" for /app/m.xyz". Extension-less files and .js files are correct now: Node's module syntax detection (on by default since 22.7) loads ./mod and ./lib.js as modules, and the container matches after the isESM change. Only a name that *has* an extension the loader does not know is wrong. Fix site: the resolution-to-format path in packages/core/src/process/executors/node/process.ts (loadModule / normalizeModule), which needs a new ResolveFailure kind from runtime/resolver.ts resolveDetailed and an ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION branch beside the not-exported and dir-target ones.

material.description: Measured 2026-10-23 by a judge (shard guest) at HEAD f5d5931. Host V8 prints the receiver: `E.methodFrame()` gives "    at Object.methodFrame (/.../main.js:30:44)" and a top-level frame "    at Object.<anonymous> (...)". The container prints "    at methodFrame (/app/main.js:31:3)" and "    at <anonymous> (/app/main.js:44:16)" -- no `Object.` receiver, and none at all where the host has `Object.<anonymous>`. Every container trace also carries three engine frames no host trace has: "    at call (native)", "    at loadCJS (owc-bootstrap.js:1006:21)" and "    at runMain (owc-bootstrap.js:1484:14)" (the line numbers move with the bootstrap source), where the host ends with its own node:internal/modules/cjs/loader frames. A try/catch stack is 5 lines against the host's 9. Recorded in Readme.md. See .gm/witness-out/owc-guest-error-stack-frame-shape.txt.
material.subject: a guest stack frame names no receiver and every guest trace ends with the container's own engine frames
material.witness: ENGINE-LIMITED, verified at HEAD c15e75b (load 12.8-20.2, 654 MB free). Three-arm differential: host node v24.15.0, the container driven by /tmp/owc-r4/probe2/run-owc-repo.mts out of packages/core, and BARE QuickJS 0.32 (quickjs-emscripten 0.32, @jitl/quickjs-wasmfile-release-sync) driven straight from node with no container around it (/tmp/owc-r5/engerr/bare/run-bare-qjs.cjs). One process per arm. The half of the row that was fixable is FIXED: a guest trace no longer carries any frame of this container's own -- the three engine frames it named (at call (native), at loadCJS (owc-bootstrap.js:...), at runMain (owc-bootstrap.js:...)) are gone and every one of the six CJS cases now ends with node's own loader frames byte-identical to the host (D1-method f6-f10: Module._compile (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1830:14), Object..js (:1961:10), Module.load (:1553:32), Module._load (:1355:12), wrapModuleLoad (:255:19)), the module body is at Object.<anonymous> and not at <anonymous>, and a try/catch stack is 11 lines against the host's 11, not 5 against 9. What remains is the receiver, and it is the engine's: new E().methodFrame() gives '    at /app/main.js:77:56' where the host gives '    at E.methodFrame (/app/main.js:77:47)'; new Foo() gives '    at Foo (/app/main.js:80:33)' where the host gives '    at new Foo (...)'; Bar.sm() gives '    at /app/main.js:83:39' where the host gives '    at Bar.sm (...)'. Bare QuickJS 0.32 with no container in the way writes '    at <anonymous> (bare.js:40:56)' for the method call, '    at <anonymous> (bare.js:45:39)' for the static call and '    at Foo (bare.js:42:33)' for the constructor -- the same frames this container is handed, so nothing here drops or mangles a name the engine wrote. A frame whose function carries a name already agrees on both sides: '    at get gg (/app/main.js:86:44)' and '    at inner (/app/main.js:88:72)'. The receiver a frame was called on is not something this engine writes into a frame it writes, so no guest-side reading of the text can put it there: recovering 'E.methodFrame' from 'at /app/main.js:77:56' would mean parsing the source at that line and column and evaluating the receiver expression, and it is undefined for obj[key]() and this.x(). Recorded rather than fixed: Readme.md, the bullet 'A guest stack frame names no receiver', rewritten with these measurements and the bare-QuickJS proof.

material.description:
Narrowed remainder of owc-engine-stack-underflow-dynamic-compile, measured 2026-10-23 against host Node 24.15.0 on the commit 28bb0d8095f74a846706b9e60b6f74c28fb194ba.

QuickJS aborts the compile of a for-of whose iterable holds a yield: `for (const x of (yield 1))`. The compatibility rewrite (rxForOfYields in runtime/guest/regex-compat.ts) hoists that iterable into a const, and that rewrite now reaches every place the container itself compiles a body at run time: new Function in any module kind (runtime/guest/loader.ts), all four vm surfaces and vm.compileFunction (runtime/guest/modules/pure-b.ts), and node -p / node --print (runtime/eval-source.ts). All of those were verified matching host Node line for line after the change.

What it does NOT reach is a string the ENGINE compiles because user code asked it to, through eval. Measured in isolation (host Node 24.15.0 vs the container, load 60-68, one container per case):

  eval('(function*(){ for (const x of (yield 1)) {} })')          host: 'function'   owc: throws InternalError: stack underflow (op=110, pc=8)
  (0, eval)('(function*(){ for (const x of (yield 1)) {} })')     host: 'function'   owc: throws InternalError: stack underflow (op=110, pc=8)
  node -e "console.log(typeof eval(<same>))"                      host: exit 0      owc: exit 1, stderr 'InternalError: stack underflow (op=110, pc=8)'

The same two lines inside an ES module fault identically. This is out of reach rather than unfixed: QuickJS grants a direct eval -- the one that reads the caller's scope -- only when the callee is the intrinsic %eval%, so any wrapper installed over globalThis.eval turns every direct eval into an indirect one and costs it the caller's scope (vm.runInContext reads its sandbox through a with-scoped direct eval, and a package that evals "require('x')" reads the module's own binding). A Proxy over eval was measured too and loses the scope the same way. Replacing eval to serve the indirect case would therefore break the direct case, which is the common one.

Witness: /tmp/owc-r4/judge-engine-goal-8/o/{triage-cjs,esm,cli}/host.out and owc.out.

material.description: Measured 2026-10-23 (judge shard fetch-web, session adv2-judge-fetch-web-8), host Node 24.15.0 against the container, one isolated differential of 97 cases run twice in the container with byte-identical stdout and empty stderr. A write to an accessor that has a getter and no setter, inside a strict-mode body, throws TypeError with the text "no setter for property" in the container and "Cannot set property <name> of #<Class> which has only a getter" on the host: e.type="y" on an Event, m.data=1 on a MessageEvent (#<_MessageEvent>), c.code=1006 on a CloseEvent (#<_CloseEvent>), r.status=201 on a Response (#<_Response>) and q.url="http://y.test/" on a Request (#<_Request>). material.subject: Out of scope of repair round 1 (verifier repro-6): QuickJS 0.32 engine divergence. In a class body, 'get' followed by a line break and then a method name parses as a field named get plus a method; V8 parses an accessor ('get foo() {}'). Example: b06-tostring/t5 prints typeof new A().foo as 'function' under OWC and 'number' under Node. Repro: /tmp/owc-r4/verify-hubesm/repro-6 (get-nl.mjs, get-nl.cjs, set-get-nl.mjs).
material.witness: ENGINE-LIMITED (QuickJS 0.32 parser), verified at HEAD c15e75b (load 12.8-20.2, 654 MB free). Three arms: host node v24.15.0, the container via /tmp/owc-r4/probe2/run-owc-repo.mts out of packages/core, and BARE QuickJS 0.32 (quickjs-emscripten 0.32, @jitl/quickjs-wasmfile-release-sync) driven straight from node with no container around it. In a CommonJS module the container prints typeof new A().foo as 'function' where the host prints 'number' (F2), and in an ES module the same class body prints 'function' where the host prints 'number' (M4); 'set' followed by a line break misparses the same way (M7-set-get-newline 'function' where the host prints 'undefined' for the set/get pair), and a blank line between 'get' and the name does too (M8 'function' against the host's 'number'). The same source with 'get' and the name on one line agrees on both sides (F4 'number', M6 'number'). BARE QuickJS 0.32 with no container in the way parses the same source the same way -- typeof new A().foo is 'function' there too against 'number' under host Node 24.15, and the same-line form is 'number' on both -- so this is the engine's own parse of a class body and not a rewrite of this container's: the source reaches the engine unchanged and QuickJS ends the class element at the line terminator where V8 does not. Recorded rather than fixed: Readme.md, the bullet 'In a class body, get or set followed by a line break is a field plus a method', which now carries the bare-QuickJS proof and this row's id. No code edited around it: a rewrite that joins 'get' to the next line would have to be right about every line terminator in every class body, and QuickJS also ends the element at a line terminator inside a /* */ comment.
